title: IFFI marks Uttam Kumar's centenary with restored 'Chowringhee' among five classics
dek: The Goa festival honoured seven film figures born in 1926 on Saturday and is screening NFDC restorations in Bengali, Hindi, Malayalam and Marathi.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa paid tribute on Saturday to seven figures of Indian cinema born in 1926, among them the Bengali star Uttam Kumar, and is screening five restored classics in Hindi, Bengali, Malayalam and Marathi to mark their birth centenaries.

The seven honoured on the festival's second day were Uttam Kumar, the Hindi filmmaker Shakti Samanta, the composer O.P. Nayyar, the Marathi actor Suryakant Mandhare, the Malayalam star Prem Nazir, the Hindi actor Raaj Kumar and the composer Ravi, known as Bombay Ravi, according to reports. The restorations were carried out by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) under the National Film Heritage Mission, a programme of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting to digitise and restore India's film archive.

## The restored films

For Uttam Kumar the festival chose Chowringhee, the Bengali film based on Sankar's novel about life in a grand Kolkata hotel, in which he plays the hotel's receptionist, Satyasundar "Sata" Bose. Festival material notes that the actor worked for more than three decades and appeared in over 200 films, including Saptapadi, Harano Sur, Nayak, Chiriyakhana and Amanush.

The other restored titles are:

- Kashmir Ki Kali, which brings together Shakti Samanta, who directed 43 feature films under his Shakti Films banner, and O.P. Nayyar's music
- Sadhi Manase, the Marathi film in which Mandhare plays a blacksmith, Shankar, with music by Lata Mangeshkar under the pseudonym Anandghan
- Thulabharam, in which Prem Nazir, who appeared in more than 700 films and received the Padma Bhushan in 1983, plays a factory worker and trade union activist, a departure from his romantic roles
- Waqt, directed by Yash Chopra, for Raaj Kumar and Bombay Ravi

## The Bengal connection

Uttam Kumar was born in Kolkata on 3 September 1926 and died in 1980. He is the only Bengali figure among the seven honoured, and Chowringhee is the festival's Bengali-language title in the restored-classics strand. The tribute puts a Kolkata story, set in one of the city's grand hotels of the period, in front of the festival's national and international audiences.

## Elsewhere at the festival

The 57th IFFI runs until 28 November across Panaji, Porvorim, Margao and Ponda under the theme "Stories Without Borders", with the filmmaker Ashutosh Gowariker as festival director. Saturday's programme also included masterclasses on parallel cinema, marking 50 years of the Kannada director Girish Kasaravalli, and on documentary film, and open-air screenings at Miramar and Vagator beaches and in Margao.

A programme marking 25 years of Gowariker's Lagaan, with the director and the film's lead actor and producer, Aamir Khan, is also on the schedule. Results of the Creative Minds of Tomorrow programme, in which 100 young filmmakers from 13 crafts compete, and of Prasar Bharati's Page to Pitch scriptwriting lab, each with a ₹5 lakh prize, are due on 24 November. The festival closes with Anthony Chen's We Are All Strangers.
